title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India

content.caseIdentity: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, (1978) 1 SCC 248
content.facts: The petitioner's passport was impounded without a prior hearing under the Passport Act, 1967.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether procedure established by law under Article 21 must be fair, just and reasonable
content.holding: Procedure established by law under Article 21 cannot be arbitrary, fanciful or oppressive. It must be fair, just and reasonable.
content.ratioDecidendi: Article 21 procedure is not satisfied by a mere enacted form. The procedure must also meet the standard of fairness associated with Articles 14 and 19 where applicable.
content.presentLegalPosition: Maneka remains the controlling reading of Article 21 procedure.
content.relevance: Maneka Gandhi is central to the modern interpretation of Article 21 and the integrated relationship of Articles 14, 19 and 21. It is commonly used to explain the development from the earlier A.K. Gopalan approach to a fairness-based reading of procedure established by law.
